unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12-LEVEL: B1.4 THEME 5: LIFE IN THE CULTURAL AND NATURAL WORLD

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''Life in the Cultural and Natural World'' with a focus on stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world and gaining awareness of climate change. They will create a multimedia presentation or visual project that highlights examples of cultural stereotypes and their impact on global understanding, alongside stories or traditions that celebrate cultural diversity. The project will also address the urgent issue of climate change, examining how diverse cultures around the world are affected by and responding to this crisis. Students will propose actionable solutions to promote cultural empathy and environmental sustainability, reflecting on the interconnectedness of humanity and nature. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the cultural and natural world with its components such as stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 12 may know what stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 12, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the cultural and natural world'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''worldwide, cultural exchange, climate, universal and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Governments should implement stricter laws to combat climate change. They could find alternative solutions to deforestation.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''stereotypes and cultural diversity in the world; gaining awareness on climate change'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about climate change and cultural diversity in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: A Panel Discussion The teacher organises a group activity simulating a panel discussion where students role-play a meeting on either ''Climate Change Awareness'' or ''Cultural Diversity in the World''. One student acts as the moderator (speaker), while other group members take on roles such as an environmental activist, a cultural expert, or a concerned community member. The moderator asks each participant prepared or spontaneous questions like, ''What steps should we take to fight with climate change?'' or ''How can we promote cultural harmony?'' Participants respond with their ideas using target vocabulary. After the discussion, the moderator summarises and reports each participant's statements to the audience using reported speech, such as: ''The activist said, ‘We must engage communities in recycling programs’, which I reported as: The activist said we must engage communities in recycling programs''. This interactive setup helps students improve vocabulary, reported speech, and collaborative communication skills. The teacher gives feedback on the accuracy of their sentences and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe cultural diversity and climate awareness in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Matching and Storytelling The teacher prepares a matching game where students match vocabulary words such as ''prejudice'', ''harmony'', and ''to recycle'' with their relevant pictures to build understanding. Once the matches are complete, students use the matched words to create a short story about either a cultural festival their family or community joined or an action their school took for climate change. For instance, students might write, ''My teacher said, ‘We should build harmony in our community’, and I reported it as: My teacher said we should build harmony in our community''. This activity integrates matching and storytelling with reported speech. Then the teacher gives feedback on their sentences and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
